01 About

I'm a digital marketer, and the part I actually do is the creative part: strategy, content, creative direction, writing the short-form video scripts, running the paid ads, and the posting itself. Everything past that runs through a team.

My clients include Habtambet, One Mobile, Orbit Electronics, Techno Z Engineering, SAF Home Decor, and TM Business — a group of five companies covering coffee, packaging, wholesale, fashion, and solar tech.

Some of that work crosses borders — campaigns written for buyers in Canada and audiences in South Sudan — and some of it is institutional: I've done marketing work for the British Council and the British Embassy in Addis Ababa.

Every account is its own set of tiles. Same hand arranging them.

04 Campaign spotlight
TikTok · Meta · Telegram

Personification of Habtambet

Created the "Habtam" mascot to give the brand a face people would recognize mid-scroll instead of another betting logo.

The problem

Betting brands in Ethiopia mostly look the same in a feed — a logo, a payout figure, a stock photo. Habtambet was competing on the same visual ground as everyone else, so nothing it posted carried past the moment someone scrolled by it.

What I did

Built a character the brand could own. Green persona, top hat, sacks of cash, always in the same world. Every post ran through him rather than around him, so the mascot became the recognisable element instead of the logo. I wrote the scripts and directed the shoots to keep him consistent across TikTok, Meta, and Telegram.

Result

12M+views in a year
146K+followers gained

Engagement lifted and, more usefully, people started recognising the character on sight — the brand stopped needing to introduce itself in every post.

Telegram

Community building for HabtamBet

Ran a Friday competition series that turned a 70,000-subscriber Telegram channel into a community with 15,000 people showing up weekly.

The problem

The Telegram channel had 70,000 subscribers and almost no activity. Subscribers are a vanity number if nobody opens the channel — the audience existed on paper only.

What I did

Gave people a standing reason to come back on a specific day. A Friday competition series, same slot every week, with mechanics simple enough to enter from the notification itself. Predictability was the point: once people knew Friday meant something, opening the channel became a habit rather than a decision.

Result

70Ksubscribers activated
15Kweekly active participants

Roughly a fifth of the channel turned into people who actually show up, which also gave the brand somewhere to launch things other than paid placement.

TikTok · Meta · Telegram

Ease of Life for Orbit Electronics

Split the content into two lanes — lifestyle storytelling and detailed product reviews — to grow reach and still answer the questions people have before buying an appliance.

The problem

Appliances are a considered purchase. Content that only chases reach brings in people who will never buy a fridge, and content that only lists specs never reaches anyone new. Doing one or the other would have cost the account either growth or sales.

What I did

Ran two funnels side by side under one idea, "Ease of Life". One lane was lifestyle storytelling built for reach — the fridge inside somebody's actual day. The other was detailed product reviews aimed at people already comparing models, answering the cooling, capacity, and warranty questions that decide the purchase. The lifestyle lane fed the review lane rather than competing with it.

Result

29Mpost views
18.9Mvideo views
4.7Mreach
110K+TikTok followers gained
1.1Mlikes
156Kshares

Across the year the account added 100,000 net followers, with a New Year's campaign built specifically to convert that reach into follows rather than just views.

05 Quill Communications

The startup I'm building

Quill Communications is the agency I run alongside my own client work. We're a team of seven, and between us we cover the full stack of digital marketing rather than just the creative end — content and production, paid media, community management, reporting, and web.

That means if a brief is bigger than one marketer, it doesn't have to go elsewhere. I take a lot of work personally, and anything past that comes through Quill.
